transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-03-04
Start: 16:00 PST
Duration: 45 minutes
Attendees: Ethan Park (Redwood AE), Maya Singh (Redwood SE), Jordan Lee (Redwood Solutions), Carlos Mendes (Valence CTO), Priya Anand (Valence Head of ML), Liam O'Neill (Valence Infra)

Summary (auto):
Valence Bank is evaluating Dedicated capacity for production LLM workloads. Key concerns: data isolation, predictable throughput for peak trading hours, burst capacity for intra-day spikes, compliance (SOC2, audit logs), KMS integration, and rolling upgrades. They currently run a mix of OpenAI-hosted models and an on-prem prototype. Next steps include pricing/SOW, SOC2 + architecture docs, and a benchmark run led by Redwood SE.

Topics: Dedicated capacity, isolation, burst strategy, autoscale, KMS/HSM, network topology (VPC/Private), SLOs and latency targets, migration plan

Action items: See metadata above.

Transcript:
00:00 Ethan (Redwood AE): Hey everyone, thanks for joining, I'm Ethan, I'm the AE working with Valence. With me is Maya, our systems engineer, and Jordan on solutions. How's everyone doing?
00:12 Carlos (Valence): Doing well, thanks. Carlos here. We got about 45 minutes, so maybe we can jump in.
00:17 Priya (Valence): Yep, Priya. We just wanna make sure we cover the throughput and the compliance bits.
00:22 Maya (Redwood SE): Great we'll focus on the Dedicated flow and then give some concrete numbers for burst and steady-state.
00:30 Ethan (Redwood AE): Quick agenda: 1) current stack & pain points, 2) target workloads and SLAs, 3) dedicated architecture options, 4) pricing and next steps. Sound good?
00:40 Liam (Valence): Sounds good.
00:45 Carlos: To start right now our ML team is using a mix of OpenAI for customer-facing chat and a small in-house cluster for internal summarization. The problem is predictable latency during peak trading hours and we need data isolation for regulated PII flows. We also need to keep cost under control the cost per token is getting insane if we don't batch or have reserved capacity.
01:02 Priya: We also have models with long context windows 32k tokens in some cases so KV cache behavior matters for us.
01:10 Maya: Understood. When you say in-house cluster, are you running on-prem GPUs or in a cloud VPC?
01:15 Carlos: It's a colo setup right now, some on-prem-ish boxes, but not production-grade orchestration. We're considering either Redwood Dedicated or fully private install.
01:25 Ethan: Good we'll talk about Dedicated first since it gives reserved GPUs and isolation without you managing the runtime. For private/on-prem we have a different path.
01:33 Liam: Two big Qs from infra: 1) can you guarantee network isolation and SAML/SSO integration? 2) How do you handle KMS and key custody?
01:43 Maya: On the isolation front, Dedicated gives you tenant-level isolation with dedicated GPU pools. Networking can be VPC peering or private link depending on cloud region. For KMS, we support customer-managed KMS and HSM integrations for keys; you can bring your own keys.
01:58 Carlos: Is there any possibility of full air-gap? We do have a subset of models that can't leave our network.
02:05 Maya: For fully air-gapped, that's in the Private deployment track we can provide an on-prem package that doesn't call home. Dedicated is logically isolated but still in our managed cloud; so if you absolutely need air-gap, Private is the route.
02:20 Priya: Latency targets for our chat use-case we need p95 under 300 ms for short responses (<=256 tokens). For long-form gen it's okay to be higher but we need throughput for batch embeddings and large runs.
02:33 Maya: That's helpful we size pools by expected concurrency and average token rate. For sub-300ms p95 on short responses, we'd recommend reserved GPUs with optimized kernels and continuous batching disabled for ultra-low latency routes; you can also pin a lower batch size for those calls.
02:50 Ethan: Can you share ballpark traffic? QPS, tokens per minute, percent of requests that need the low-latency path?
02:58 Carlos: We're looking at steady-state 60 qps for short responses, peaking to 250 qps during market open windows for a 20-30 minute window. About 30% of calls are low-latency chat and 70% are embeddings/summarizations that can tolerate higher latency.
03:16 Maya: Ok, that spike is doable with burst capacity. Our Dedicated model supports reserved baseline plus burstable nodes for short windows. There are two approaches: autoscale with warm standby nodes or pre-provisioned burst capacity that you reserve for peak windows. The first is cheaper but slower to warm, second is more expensive but gives predictable perf.
03:40 Liam: How fast is warm up for the autoscale option? We can't afford multi-minute delays when the market opens.
03:46 Maya: Warmup depends if model weights are already on disk and instance types are warmed, it can be under 60s for typical models. For cold starts where instances need to download and load models and warm caches, it can be 2-5 minutes. That's why we recommend warm standby for market open.
04:05 Carlos: So we'd probably want a baseline reserved pool sized for steady traffic plus a small warm standby for the opens.
04:12 Ethan: Exactly, and we can propose pricing that mixes reserved baseline with a short-term burst reservation for the two daily spikes.
04:18 Priya: About the KV cache when you do rollouts or scale out, how is KV cache shared? We can't afford cache thrash on scale events.
04:27 Maya: Good question. Our runtime supports distributed KV sharding and sticky routing so active sessions can be routed to nodes with local KV cache; we also offer a shared prefix cache option for frequently used prefixes. There is some loss on scale events, but with sticky routing and session affinity it's minimized.
04:47 Priya: Okay, that addresses a lot. What about model variants and quantization do you handle mixed precision or quantized weights to balance cost and latency?
04:55 Maya: Yes, Redwood Optimize provides recommended quantization profiles per model and workload. For Dedicated we can pre-deploy FP16 or 4-bit quant variants depending on quality requirements. We'll surface the latency/cost tradeoffs in the benchmark.
05:08 Carlos: Security audit logs and retention. We need immutable audit logs for model access and inference events for 7 years for regulatory reasons.
05:18 Maya: We can export audit logs to your SIEM. For Dedicated, logs are tenant scoped, and we support long-term retention via object store and integration with your archival policies. We'll include options in the SOW.
05:30 Liam: How about SSO and RBAC? We have Okta.
05:33 Ethan: We support SAML/OIDC and can federate to Okta. Role-based access and scoped API keys are standard.
05:39 Priya: And encryption in transit and at rest?
05:41 Maya: TLS in transit, and at-rest encryption using either Redwood-managed keys or customer KMS. For HSM-backed keys, we support common HSM vendors via KMS integration.
05:50 Carlos: Excellent. Competitors we have internal evaluation of Anthropic and OpenAI for chat, and AWS SageMaker for hosting. How do you compare on price and latency?
06:02 Ethan: High-level: Redwood aims to beat public-per-token economics once you hit steady-state with reserved capacity because we optimize kernel selection and batching at runtime; Dedicated also avoids multi-tenant interference. Latency for short responses is comparable or better than hosted providers when pinned. We'll share benchmark numbers from similar financial customers.
06:20 Priya: Can you run a benchmark using our prompt set and models (we may want to use a custom finetuned open model)?
06:25 Maya: Absolutely that's the plan. We'll provision a Dedicated trial cluster, run a benchmark with your prompt set, and measure p50/p95/p99 and token cost. We need your sample prompts, approximate average lengths, and any finetuned model artifacts or model config pointers.
06:38 Carlos: We can share a sanitized prompt set. Also need to know about data residency can logs be kept in eu-west-1 for our eu customers?
06:46 Maya: Yes, we have region-specific deployments. For Dedicated we can pin the deployment to a region. For Private we can do on-prem/eu only.
06:55 Liam: Operations question: how are OS and runtime upgrades handled? We can't have noisy rolling upgrades during market hours.
07:02 Maya: We support scheduled maintenance windows. For Dedicated customers we coordinate canary rollouts and allow you to define blackout windows (e.g., market hours). We also offer automatic fallback policies to older model variants if a rollout causes regressions.
07:16 Ethan: Any questions on pricing model? We charge for reserved GPU capacity (monthly commit), plus optional burst reservations and data egress. There's also a platform fee for enterprise support and long-term retention. We'll include detailed numbers in the SOW.
07:30 Carlos: Can you give a rough monthly for baseline we discussed say 60 qps steady with 250 qps peaks?
07:36 Ethan: Ballpark assuming a mix of L4-style GPUs and quantized models, baseline reserved pool could be in the 6-10 GPU range depending on model and concurrency. Monthly commit would be $60k-$120k depending on model sizes and support. Burst reservations for the peaks would be an additional line item. We'll flesh this in the pricing doc.
07:52 Priya: That price range is reasonable as a starting point. We'll need SSO and SOC2 docs before legal gets involved.
07:59 Ethan: Absolutely, I'll send SOC2 artifacts and our architecture diagram.
08:03 Carlos: On contract we prefer annual reserved with quarterly review. Do you offer committed throughput discounts?
08:09 Ethan: Yes, annual committed reserved capacity gets better unit pricing and priority for burst capacity. We'll include both monthly and annual options in the SOW.
08:18 Priya: For the benchmark, can you emulate our traffic pattern with the open model plus our finetuned checkpoint?
08:24 Maya: We'll need your model artifact or container, or we can host an equivalent open model and apply your finetuned checkpoint if you can share it. We'll sign an NDA for artifacts.
08:33 Carlos: NDA is already in place for the RFI stage, but we'll loop in legal if needed.
08:38 Jordan (Redwood Solutions): For the POC, typical cadence we've done: 1) get sanitized prompt set & sample model, 2) Redwood stages a Dedicated trial cluster for 1-2 weeks, 3) run benchmarks + QA, 4) review results and tune quant/instance mix, 5) propose SOW.
08:56 Liam: How does billing work for a trial cluster?
08:59 Ethan: Trials are usually billed as short-term reserved capacity at a reduced rate or as credits depending on negotiation. We'll cover that in the SOW.
09:07 Priya: Any known gotchas? For example, do you throttle embeddings differently than chat?
09:12 Maya: Embeddings are handled differently; we recommend separate routes and separate instance pools for embeddings-heavy workloads to avoid interference with low-latency chat. We can set rate limits and dedicated embedding nodes.
09:24 Carlos: What about model rollbacks if a new model causes a regression, what's the fallback time?
09:29 Maya: We have automatic fallback routing; rollback can be immediate at the control plane level. If artifacts are already deployed, traffic can switch in seconds; if a model needs to be reloaded, it depends on warm caches but control-plane failover is near-instant.
09:44 Priya: For SIEM integration and log formats do you ship structured inference logs with token-level metadata?
09:51 Maya: We can export structured logs including request/response metadata, latency, token counts, and model/version ids. For PII-sensitive flows you can opt to redact or not store full prompts.
10:03 Carlos: Okay let's talk timeline. Our compliance review and procurement team's window is end of Q2 ideally we'd be in pilot by mid-April. Does that align with your expected ramp?
10:14 Ethan: Yes, that's feasible. We can aim for a pilot in April. Key sequence: finalize SOW and pricing this week, kick off SE benchmark in early March, review and iterate, then pilot in April.
10:27 Priya: Can you send the SOC2 and the network diagram today?
10:31 Ethan: I can get that out after this call.
10:34 Carlos: Anything else?
10:36 Liam: One more infra nit: do you support private link endpoints and static IP egress?
10:41 Maya: Yes private link and static egress IPs are supported for Dedicated. We'll provide the VPC architecture options in the doc.
10:48 Priya: Also please include model quantization tradeoff matrix in the benchmark report.
10:52 Maya: Will do.
10:55 Ethan: Alright, recap and next steps: Ethan will send pricing + draft SOW, SOC2 and network diagram; Maya will prep benchmark plan and propose dates for the trial cluster (aiming for ~2026-03-10 kick-off); Carlos to share sanitized prompt set and compliance contacts. We'll reconvene after benchmark results.
11:12 Carlos: Thanks everyone, this was helpful.
11:16 Priya: Thanks.
11:18 Ethan: Thanks, talk soon.
11:20 End meeting.
